System and method

Formula, charge and spin, method, basis and solvent of the calculation.

Quantity Value
Formula \mathrm{C_{6}H_{6}}
Charge q 0
Spin multiplicity 2S+1 1
Method RBLYP
Basis set 6\text{-}31\mathrm{G}(d,p)
Atoms 12
Point group used by Gaussian C_{2v}
Framework group \mathrm{C_{2}H_{2}} in the \sigma_v plane; \mathrm{C_{4}H_{4}} in general positions
Point group of the geometry D_{6h}
Basis functions 120
Independent functions 120
Alpha electrons N_\alpha 21
Beta electrons N_\beta 21
Closed shell
Exact-exchange fraction c_{\mathrm{HF}} 0.4627
Rotational constants (A,B,C) (5.72573, 5.72573, 2.86287)\,\mathrm{GHz}

Where these values come from:

  • N_\alpha and N_\beta count spin-up and spin-down electrons; together they are the nuclear charges Z_A minus the charge q.
  • Their difference fixes the spin projection M_S=(N_\alpha-N_\beta)/2; the usual highest-weight input has S=M_S.
  • Closed shells have doubly occupied orbitals; equal spin counts alone do not establish one.
  • In a hybrid functional, c_{\mathrm{HF}} weights exact Hartree–Fock exchange; the density functional supplies the rest.
  • Each rotational constant follows from a principal moment of inertia I.

N_\alpha+N_\beta=\sum_A Z_A-q,\qquad 2S+1=N_\alpha-N_\beta+1,\qquad E_{\mathrm{XC}}=c_{\mathrm{HF}}\,E_{\mathrm{X}}^{\mathrm{HF}}+E_{\mathrm{X}}^{\mathrm{DFT}}+E_{\mathrm{C}}^{\mathrm{DFT}},\qquad B=\frac{h}{8\pi^{2}I}

Energy components

Components of the converged electronic energy describe the whole molecule. Unreported terms are omitted.

Quantity Value
Orbital kinetic energy T 6263.95140974\,\mathrm{eV}
Electron–nuclear term V_{\mathrm{ne}} -25718.3852881\,\mathrm{eV}
Coulomb and exchange–correlation J+E_{\mathrm{XC}} 7600.09454628\,\mathrm{eV}
Nuclear repulsion E_{\mathrm{nn}} 5548.34995134\,\mathrm{eV}
Electronic energy E_{\mathrm{el}} -6305.98938079\,\mathrm{eV}
Virial ratio -V/T 2.0067

For an all-electron calculation without additional model terms:

E_{\mathrm{el}}=T+V_{\mathrm{ne}}+J+E_{\mathrm X}+E_{\mathrm C}+E_{\mathrm{nn}}

  • T is the orbital kinetic energy, T_s in Kohn–Sham DFT.
  • J+E_{\mathrm X}+E_{\mathrm C} is one printed term; separating them requires a matching-density evaluation or explicit output.
  • -V/T is a virial diagnostic, not an accuracy test. Additional model terms require separate contributions.

Frontier orbitals

The orbital gap is not an optical excitation energy:

\Delta\epsilon=\epsilon_{\mathrm{LUMO}}-\epsilon_{\mathrm{HOMO}}

Quantity Energy [\mathrm{eV}]
HOMO energy \epsilon_{\mathrm{HOMO}}, 1e_{1g} -7.4112
LUMO energy \epsilon_{\mathrm{LUMO}}, 1e_{2u} 1.466
HOMO–LUMO gap \Delta\epsilon 8.8772

Canonical orbital energies near the gap; degenerate components have separate levels. Labels use D_{6h} symmetry: lowercase for orbitals, capitals for states. Gaussian computed in C_{2v}, so the labels it printed belong to that group.

Frontier orbitals, selectable by snapshot:

  • The HOMO and LUMO include symmetry, character and energy.
  • Red surfaces enclose \psi<-0.02\,a_0^{\frac{-3}{2}}; blue surfaces enclose \psi>+0.02\,a_0^{\frac{-3}{2}}.

Atomic charges and electric moments

Mulliken charges for the final evaluated geometry, when a matching SCF population analysis was printed:

  • Red atoms carry q_A<0, blue ones q_A>0 and white ones q_A\approx0, on a scale symmetric about zero.
  • Hovering over an atom shows its q_A.
  • Mulliken populations split shared density equally; \mathbf P is the density matrix and \mathbf S the overlap matrix.
  • The split depends on the basis set, so compare charges only within one method and basis.

q_A=Z_A-\sum_{\mu\in A}(\mathbf{P}\mathbf{S})_{\mu\mu}

The dipole moment of the same density, in its printed orientation:

\boldsymbol{\mu}=\begin{pmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{pmatrix}\,\mathrm{D}=\begin{pmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{pmatrix}\,e a_0,\qquad |\boldsymbol{\mu}|=0\,\mathrm{D}=0\,e a_0

The traceless quadrupole moment of the same density, in atomic units and debye ångström:

\mathbf{Q}=\begin{pmatrix}1.84671 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1.84669 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3.6934\end{pmatrix}\,\mathrm{e}\,a_0^{2}=\begin{pmatrix}2.48389 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2.48387 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4.96775\end{pmatrix}\,\mathrm{D}\,\mathrm{\AA}

Geometry optimization

Gaussian printed 1 convergence checks, shown in output order, with circles for maxima, squares for RMS values, colour for each criterion’s pass or fail, and a dashed line across the plot for each limit, long dashes for the maximum and short for the RMS.

  • Each energy E_n is measured from that of the last check printed, E_n-E_N, which is not assumed converged.
  • The forces are given by their largest value, F_{\max}=\max_i\lvert F_i\rvert, and their root mean square, F_{\mathrm{RMS}}=\sqrt{\tfrac{1}{N}\sum_i F_i^2}.
  • Displacements \Delta q are in bohr for distances and radians for angles.

Vibrational frequencies

The latest analysis has 30 modes, including 0 imaginary, with real-mode IR intensities shown against approximate mid-infrared regions as dashed lines, and frequencies unscaled unless stated.

  • Each wavenumber follows from the mode’s force constant and reduced mass, \tilde{\nu}_k=\frac{1}{2\pi c}\sqrt{k_k/\mu_k}.
  • The IR intensity grows with the squared change of the dipole along the mode, I_k\propto\lvert\partial\boldsymbol{\mu}/\partial Q_k\rvert^2.
  • A mode is imaginary when k_k<0, a direction of negative curvature.

In D_{6h} only modes that change the dipole absorb in the infrared:

  • Infrared-active symmetries are a_{2u} (z), e_{1u} (x,y).
  • Every other mode has zero intensity.
Normal-mode frequencies

Modes are ordered by frequency. Negative wavenumbers mark imaginary modes, not absorption frequencies.

Normal-mode animations

The viewer animates imaginary modes, the six lowest real modes and the four most IR-intense modes, each scaled so its largest atomic displacement amplitude is \max_A\lVert\mathbf{u}_{kA}\rVert=0.6\,\mathrm{\AA}, where \mathbf{u}_{kA} is the amplitude vector of atom A in mode k.
